{{Short description|Element of the representation ring}}
In mathematics, the '''Bott cannibalistic class''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Raoul|last=Bott|year=1962|authorlink=Raoul Bott}}, is an  element <math>\theta_k(V)</math> of the [[representation ring]] of a [[compact Lie group]] that describes the action of the [[Adams operation]] <math>\psi^k</math> on the [[Thom class]] <math>\lambda_V</math> of a complex [[Representation of a Lie group|representation]] <math>V</math>. The term "cannibalistic" for these classes was introduced by Frank Adams.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Adams |first=J.F. |date=April 1965 |title=On the groups J ( X )—II |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0040938365900406 |journal=Topology |language=en |volume=3 |issue=2 |pages=137–171 |doi=10.1016/0040-9383(65)90040-6|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
